summary.one_liner: Westworld is an experimental Python library for building and running multi-agent simulations of environments with interacting agents, inspired by Unity and Unity ML Agents.
summary.what_it_does: The library provides tools to create grid and non-grid simulation environments populated with agents, obstacles, collectibles and triggers. Objects can be subclassed to make custom types, and a spawner can place them randomly. All objects share a basic rigid body system, and agents have simple behaviors such as pathfinding, wandering, random walk, fleeing and vision range. It includes automatic maze generation and a layer feature that converts an image into obstacles snapped to a grid. Simulations can be visualized with PyGame, replayed, and exported as GIF or video. The README says optimization can use heuristics or Reinforcement Learning, though RL integration with Stable Baselines is listed as a roadmap item.
use_cases: multi-agent simulation for retail or epidemiology
prototype agent pathfinding and wandering behaviors
generate random mazes for agent experiments
export simulation runs as gif or video
how_to_run: git clone the repository and run: poetry install (for developers)
notable: Grid and non-grid spatial environments with pre-coded agent behaviors
Layer integration converts images into grid-snapped obstacles
Simulation replay and export to gif or video
caveats: Explicitly experimental alpha release; documentation may be out of date and not all features tested
Roadmap items such as Reinforcement Learning integration and web visualization are not yet available
